title: Long-term evidence for mood stabilizers
bottleneck: Lithium, valproate, and other mood stabilizers are prescribed for years or decades, yet almost no randomized trials test long-term prophylactic efficacy with modern standards; lithium's anti-suicidal signal comes from observational and small-trial data, and its renal and thyroid risks accumulate over exactly the timescales that matter.
why_it_blocks: Bipolar disorder is a lifelong illness managed with lifelong drugs whose lifelong evidence base barely exists. Patients and clinicians are flying on short-term data for a long-term disease.
current_state: Lithium remains first-line in guidelines based on the best available (imperfect) evidence. Long-term comparative effectiveness research is scarce because such trials are expensive and commercially unattractive. Pragmatic registry trials and decades-long cohort studies are the only feasible design for lifelong drugs, but funders rarely support them, leaving guidelines to rest on aging evidence.
